summary: Hotfix verification for Sprint 6.1.4 packages/shared enum strip-only SyntaxError. Verified that @cts/shared now resolves to compiled dist JS and NestJS API bootstraps cleanly without the enum SyntaxError.

verification_details.nest_bootstrap: Nest started, AppModule + all ~35 modules initialized, routes mapped (/auth, /users, /health, /trading-accounts, /strategies, /followers, /subscriptions, /admin/*, /brokers/zerodha|fyers|shoonya, /instruments, etc.) - PASS
verification_details.enum_syntaxerror_absent: grep for ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX / strip-only / 'enum is not supported' / SyntaxError from shared => 0 matches - PASS
verification_details.expected_downstream_errors_ignored: ioredis ECONNREFUSED and Prisma DATABASE_URL errors are expected per environment note and unrelated to this hotfix

critical_code_review_comments: Consider adding a CI check that fails if any workspace package's main points to a .ts file to prevent regression of this class of bug.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Hotfix verified at module-load layer only. Postgres/Redis are intentionally not running in this pod; expected ioredis ECONNREFUSED and Prisma DATABASE_URL errors will appear AFTER Nest bootstrap and are NOT regressions.
rca of the issue: Node's native TS support (strip-only, no code emit) cannot handle `enum` because enums require runtime object generation. @cts/shared package.json previously pointed main/types to ./src/index.ts (raw TS with enums), so importers would load .ts directly and Node would throw ERR_UNSUPPORTED_TYPESCRIPT_SYNTAX. Fix: added tsc build emitting dist/index.js (with transpiled enums like `Broker["ZERODHA"]="ZERODHA"`) + dist/index.d.ts, and repointed main/types/exports to ./dist. Verified require.resolve returns compiled JS and Nest bootstraps without the SyntaxError.
